thread:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SMART-ROUTING-EU - sustained 5xx spike (avg 18%) across EU edge for the past 7m. Auto-fallback triggered to us-west2. Alert: SMART-ROUTER.policy.fallback.count > 50

maya_oncall: Ack. I'm on it. Paging @chris_sre for routing policy check.

chris_sre: taking. First glance: a bunch of clients hitting eu-edge endpoints resolving to old geo-records. dig shows stale A records for eu-edge-1 that point to decommissioned backend IPs. Suspect DNS propagation + low TTL rollback didn't catch up -> smart-router keeps failing over -> fallback loop to us-west2 -> cross-reg latency + throttles.

maya_oncall: can you paste the dig + sample 5xx logs?

chris_sre: paste:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> eu-edge-1.redwood.edge
;; ANSWER SECTION:
eu-edge-1.redwood.edge.  86400 IN A 203.0.113.45
eu-edge-1.redwood.edge.  86400 IN A 198.51.100.12
```
logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-15T20:12:03Z] router=smart-1 route=eu-edge -> backend=203.0.113.45 status=502 conn_err read_timeout
[2026-03-15T20:12:05Z] router=smart-1 fallback=us-west2 reason=policy_mismatch model_variant=redwood-light v=2 status=503
```

alex_dev: re TTL: looks like DNS owner accidentally pushed TTL=86400 (24h) yesterday during a zone migration. That explains the stale endpoints.

maya_oncall: ugh. So two things we should do: 1) stop the fallback loop by disabling automatic region fallback for SMART-ROUTER.policy *immediately*; 2) force failover to eu-secondary pool with manual routing overrides while DNS clears. I'll run 1) now.

chris_sre: +1. When you disable fallback, the runtime will stop redirecting to us-west2 but clients hitting stale IPs may still 502. Need cache purge + clear edge cache of old endpoints and update route table to use canonical hostnames instead of cached records.

maya_oncall: running command to update policy (console rollback):
```
# temporarily disable automatic fallback
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/policies/SMART-ROUTER/actions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"action": "disable_fallback","reason":"DNS stale endpoints causing loop - emergency"}'
```

infra_bot: deploybot: policy update accepted by controller. change_id=chg_20260315_001

maya_oncall: ok change id looks applied. Confirming metrics... fallback_count dropped within 30s. Still seeing 502s for some customers.

sam_support: heads up — support is getting multiple tickets from EU customers complaining about heavy latencies and errors. We're preparing a status message draft.

solutions_eng: paste short customer-facing blurb for status page please. Keep it clear: no technical jargon.

sam_support: draft: "We are investigating increased errors and latency for users in Europe. Some requests are being routed to an unintended region due to stale DNS records; we're applying mitigations. No data loss. We will update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?

maya_oncall: good. Add ETA to next update and mention mitigation active. I'll post.

chris_sre: next action: purge edge DNS cache + request registry owner to lower TTL. Running purge command for eu-edge prefix.

maya_oncall: purge command:
```
# purge edge hostname cache
rtrctl --cluster=eu --action=purge-host --host=eu-edge-1.redwood.edge
```

infra_bot: rtrctl: purge job queued job_id=purge_7745

chris_sre: also created a temporary routing override to send traffic to eu-secondary-pool that resolves via current canonical IPs (not zone DNS). This bypass will help while DNS TTLs expire. override_id=ovr_20260315_eu_sec

alex_dev: contacting DNS provider support to request immediate cache flush and reduce TTL to 60s. Email to provider sent (ticket #DNS-8891). ETA 20-40m.

maya_oncall: good. @sam_support — please post the status update now with the draft. Mark impacted customers (EU region) and note mitigations.

sam_support: posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-15-eu-routing (include link in replies).

solutions_eng: any customer escalations we should proactively reach out to? We should contact top 10 paying EU customers. I'll start the list and hand to CSMs.

chris_sre: monitoring: errors trending down after policy disable + override. still ~3% 5xx for requests hitting old IPs but overall latency returning to normal.

maya_oncall: handoff plan: I'm on for another 25m; if we still have >1% errors at handoff time, I will escalate to oncall-night. Otherwise we'll keep watch. Preparing notes for handoff.

alex_dev: created quick runbook snippet in the thread for night oncall:
```
1) Check metrics: /dashboards/smart-router/eu
2) If fallback_count > 5/min: re-enable manual override or contact DNS provider
3) Purge host cache: rtrctl --cluster=eu --action=purge-host --host=eu-edge-1.redwood.edge
4) Revert policy only after DNS TTL <= 120s and sanity checks
```

maya_oncall: adding one more: if customers still impacted after 60m, escalate to legal/ops for SLA credits review and runbook for customer communications.

infra_bot: dns provider status: ticket DNS-8891 updated: provider accepted flush; propagation estimated 18-30 minutes.

chris_sre: quick root cause note: human error in zone migration left TTL at 86400. Routing runtime cached resolution and policy fallback amplified it into a cross-region fallback loop. Action items: 1) enforce TTL change policy in infra templates, 2) add smart-router guardrail to detect long TTLs and avoid fallback loops, 3) test zone-flips in staging with synthetic traffic.

maya_oncall: agreed. We'll open follow-up tasks in postmortem. For now, I'm going to monitor for 30 more minutes and then handoff to @alex_dev with notes.

sam_support: customers notified, support queue triaged. No high-priority escalations yet.

alex_dev: I'm ready to take over at +30. Leave any ephemeral tokens/commands in the runbook.

maya_oncall: handing off now. Summary for handoff -> incident_bot: SMART-ROUTING-EU: fallback loop caused by stale DNS TTLs. Mitigations applied: disabled auto-fallback, edge purge queued, routing override to eu-secondary, contacting DNS provider. Customer comms posted. Monitor until DNS propagation confirmed then revert.

alex_dev: ack — taking over. I'll keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

incident_bot: Incident update recorded. severity=sev2, incident_id=INC-20260315-07, owner=alex_dev, sla-impact=partial_degradation_eu

maya_oncall: thanks team. Please add any logs or weirdness you see to INC-20260315-07. Postmortem owners: @chris_sre + @eva_platform.

eva_platform: noted, I'll start the postmortem template and link it once started.

chris_sre: leaving final note: watch model routing variants — we saw one case where fallback picked a different model_variant (redwood-light v2) which increased error surface. We'll include routing->model mapping check in postmortem.

alex_dev: 20m later: metrics show error rate <0.5% and latency normalized. DNS provider confirms flush and TTL set to 60s. Planning to remove manual override when TTL consistent.

alex_dev: 38m later: removed manual override per runbook. Re-enabled automatic fallback at 39m after TTL stable. Monitoring continues.

incident_bot: Incident INC-20260315-07 status: mitigated -> monitoring. timestamp=1887655000
